data.content:
Impressions of Theophraustus such George Eliot
The book 'Impressions of Theophraustus such George Eliot' contains the analysis of Theophraustus.

MDCCCLXXIX
MDCCCLXXIX is the year 1879, when the book was published.

Theophraustus
Theophraustus is the subject of the book 'Impressions of Theophraustus such George Eliot'.

George Eliot
George Eliot is an English author referenced in the book title.

Phaedrus
Phaedrus is a fictional character referenced in the text.

PGDP
http://www.pgdp.net is a website that hosts the text.

The Country
The Country is the place from which Canadians departed.

British Army Officers
British Army Officers are a group of military personnel from Britain who appeared benevolent in comparison to others.

Canada
Canada is the country from which Canadians departed and received facilities to support their departure.

Good Feeling
Good Feeling represents a positive sentiment or goodwill evidenced between the British Army Officers and Canadians.

Canadians
Canadians are individuals who left the country and were provided facilities for doing so.

Huge Hotels
Huge Hotels are large lodging establishments that the narrator group intends to avoid.

Fashionable Towns
Fashionable Towns are stylish urban areas that the narrator group intends to avoid.

Life
Life refers to human existence and experiences the narrator group wishes to study in simplicity.

Simplicity
Simplicity denotes a simple, uncomplicated way of living that the narrator group considers essential for studying life.

Humble Feminine Way
Humble Feminine Way represents a modest, womanly approach to achieving happiness that the narrator group aspires to follow.

We
We refers to the narrator group who will avoid large hotels, study life simply, and seek happiness in a humble, feminine manner.
